verdict.outcome_basis: readout: "terminate the Phase 3 trial of the investigational medicine evacetrapib, due to insufficient efficacy terminate the Phase 3 trial of the inv" (announcement:accelerate)
verdict.consistency: calculator expected success with 54% probability; the actual result falls in the remaining 46%

report.headline: The ACCELERATE trial of evacetrapib was stopped for futility in ~12,092 high-risk vascular patients, confirming that CETP inhibition does not reduce cardiovascular events despite large HDL-C increases.
report.summary: ACCELERATE randomized 12,092 patients with high-risk vascular disease to evacetrapib 130 mg or placebo on background statin therapy, targeting a composite of CV death, MI, stroke, coronary revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable angina with 1,670 planned events. The independent DMC stopped the trial early on October 12, 2015 for insufficient efficacy, with no safety signal. The calculator predicted a 54% probability of success (expected HR 0.904) based on phase 2 LDL-C lowering of -23% at 100 mg monotherapy, but the true placebo-adjusted effect at the 130 mg phase 3 dose is unknown; within-arm changes showed LDL-C -14% to -36% and HDL-C +54% to +129%. Human genetics available at trial start showed zero CETP studies before the 2015 cutoff, and the intended biomarker (HDL-C) is not causal for CVD. The failure is best explained by biomarker_not_causal (HDL-C elevation does not translate to benefit) compounded by effect_too_small (modest LDL-C lowering at trial dose) and insufficient_data (no placebo-adjusted phase 3 biomarker data).
key_evidence: 12,092 patients randomized (Lilly to Discontinue Development of Evacetrapib for High-Risk Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease (Oct 12, 2015); ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01687998 ACCELERATE; Assessment of the clinical effects of cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibition with evacetrapib in patients at high-risk for vascular outcomes: Rationale and design of the ACCELERATE trial)

1,670 planned primary endpoint events (Assessment of the clinical effects of cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibition with evacetrapib in patients at high-risk for vascular outcomes: Rationale and design of the ACCELERATE trial)

Primary endpoint: composite of CV death, MI, stroke, coronary revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable angina (Assessment of the clinical effects of cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibition with evacetrapib in patients at high-risk for vascular outcomes: Rationale and design of the ACCELERATE trial; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01687998 ACCELERATE)
Trial stopped early by DMC for futility on Oct 12, 2015, no safety signal (Lilly to Discontinue Development of Evacetrapib for High-Risk Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease (Oct 12, 2015))

Phase 2: evacetrapib 130 mg increased HDL-C by 129% (within-arm) and 103% vs active comparator (atorvastatin alone) (Assessment of the clinical effects of cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibition with evacetrapib in patients at high-risk for vascular outcomes: Rationale and design of the ACCELERATE trial; Efficacy, safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetic profile of evacetrapib administered as monotherapy or in combination with atorvastatin in Japanese patients with dyslipidemia)

Phase 2 placebo-adjusted LDL-C lowering -15% at 100 mg + atorvastatin (Efficacy, safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetic profile of evacetrapib administered as monotherapy or in combination with atorvastatin in Japanese patients with dyslipidemia)
Calculator predicted 54% probability of success (HR 0.904) based on LDL-C -23% from phase 2 monotherapy 100 mg; trial failed for futility (calculator; verdict)
CETP genetic association score 0.736 but zero genetic evidence items before 2015-10-12 cutoff (opentargets:CETP)

No off-target harm: no QT prolongation, no clinically relevant BP effects (Effects of the cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibitor evacetrapib on lipoproteins, apolipoproteins and 24-h ambulatory blood pressure in healthy adults; Evacetrapib at a supratherapeutic steady state concentration does not prolong QT in a thorough QT/QTc study in healthy participants)
report.what_would_change_this: Placebo-adjusted LDL-C, apoB, and SBP changes at the therapeutic 130 mg dose from the ACCELERATE phase 3 dataset (not publicly available) would clarify the true magnitude of causal biomarker modulation. Consistent Mendelian randomization evidence linking CETP inhibition to CAD risk reduction independent of HDL-C would strengthen target validation.
report.readthrough_note: Other CETP inhibitors have shown mixed results: torcetrapib failed due to off-target toxicity, dalcetrapib failed for futility, while anacetrapib demonstrated modest CV benefit primarily via LDL-C lowering. The ACCELERATE result reinforces that HDL-C elevation alone is not sufficient for CV risk reduction.

checks.detail: Open Targets genetic association 0.736 for CETP
intended biomarker HDL-C is NOT causal; LDL-equivalent change 0.858 mmol/L via LDL-C
expected HR 0.904 at 1.5 y (relative risk reduction 9.6%)
power 54% with 1670 events; smallest detectable HR 0.872

notes: systolic BP +1.69 mmHg adds HR x1.022

mechanism.target_genetics_rationale: CETP genetic association score 0.736 for coronary artery disease, but all 13 Open Targets studies published after 2015-10-12 cutoff (evidence_before_cutoff=0). CETP is well-studied; no genetic evidence before cutoff → uncertain per rules.
mechanism.notes: LDL-C: Used monotherapy placebo-adjusted -23% at 100 mg (f_e8208ef8b44ffb) per critic guidance; combination data (f_58aadd0f20c7b8) not verified as placebo-adjusted. Baseline from phase 2 (144.3 mg/dL, f_4282ceed19784f). Trial dose 130 mg on statin; monotherapy not on statin. HDL-C: Used active-comparator-adjusted combination 103% at 100 mg + atorvastatin 10 mg (f_5677129c1c8864); comparator is atorvastatin alone (active), not placebo. Baseline from phase 2 (55.1 mg/dL, f_4ca07a484eec43). Trial dose 130 mg. apoB: Only supratherapeutic data (600 mg, Day 14); used -26.1% (f_5d42a0b83c3256) but conflicting fact f_8f3e81746e8b98 shows +80.5% (same metadata). No apoB baseline available. SBP: Supratherapeutic 600 mg, Day 14 (f_049dd7f5983efe). Trial stopped early for futility (f_4657510a19768e, f_a92d2049d72b37); actual events not reported in facts, used planned 1670 (f_7262d7298b3588). Median follow-up 1.5 years (f_13d6532df5671c).

for.text: The intended biomarker was HDL-C. Evacetrapib raised HDL-C massively: +103% vs active comparator (atorvastatin alone) in phase 2 combination (f_5677129c1c8864), +129% and +54% within-arm in phase 3 at 130 mg (f_02746d884f6ab5, f_fde73e34804c2b). Yet the trial failed for insufficient efficacy (f_a92d2049d72b37).

Human genetics: CETP genetic association score 0.736 for CAD but evidence_before_cutoff = 0 (all 13 studies published after 2015-10-12) (f_ff8d155f87441a). At trial launch, no genetic evidence supported CETP inhibition as causal for CAD reduction. The calculator's secondary category flagged 'biomarker_not_causal'.

against.text: Evacetrapib also lowered LDL-C (phase 2 monotherapy -23% at 100 mg, f_e8208ef8b44ffb; phase 3 within-arm -14% to -36% at 130 mg, f_342c58c5ac1a94, f_fdb5153ab0027b) and apoB (-26.1% at supratherapeutic dose, f_5d42a0b83c3256). LDL-C/apoB lowering is causal, so some benefit was expected.

hypotheses.would_settle: Mendelian randomization of CETP variants on CAD outcomes (published after 2015) showing null effect despite HDL-C elevation; or a CETP inhibitor trial with adequate LDL-C lowering powered for outcomes.

for.text: Target genetics uncertain: CETP genetic association score 0.736 but zero studies before 2015-10-12 cutoff (f_ff8d155f87441a). The calculator's weakest_link noted 'target genetics: uncertain'. At trial initiation, human genetics did not support CETP as a causal target for CAD.

against.text: Post-2015 genetic studies (not available at trial start) show CETP variants associate with CAD, but direction and magnitude debated. The target may have some causal role but not via HDL-C.

hypotheses.would_settle: Consistent Mendelian randomization evidence linking CETP inhibition to CAD risk reduction independent of HDL-C.

for.text: Calculator expected HR 0.904 (9.6% RRR) based on LDL-C -23% from phase 2 monotherapy 100 mg (f_e8208ef8b44ffb), giving only 54% power with 1670 events and 1.5 yr follow-up (calculator). MDE HR for 80% power was 0.872. The true placebo-adjusted LDL-C lowering at 130 mg in phase 3 is unknown (only within-arm -14% to -36%, f_342c58c5ac1a94, f_fdb5153ab0027b). If true effect is smaller, power drops further.

Phase 2 combination data (100 mg + atorvastatin) used for HDL-C (+103%, f_5677129c1c8864) was active-comparator-adjusted (vs atorvastatin alone), not placebo-adjusted, per verifier. The LDL-C -15% from same study (f_58aadd0f20c7b8) has same caveat. Calculator used monotherapy LDL-C data instead.

against.text: If phase 3 within-arm LDL-C -36% (f_fdb5153ab0027b) approximates true effect, expected HR would be ~0.85, giving >80% power. But within-arm changes overestimate placebo-adjusted effect.

hypotheses.would_settle: Placebo-adjusted LDL-C and apoB changes at 130 mg from ACCELERATE phase 3 (not publicly available; would require FDA review or full publication).

for.text: SBP increase +1.69 mmHg at supratherapeutic 600 mg Day 14 (f_049dd7f5983efe). Calculator applied BP factor 1.022 (HR x1.022).

against.text: Phase 2 readout: 'devoid of clinically relevant effects on blood pressure' at 600 mg (f_5569a44aa98530). No QT prolongation at 1200 mg (f_d240660bf76467, f_e728ac2b6715d3). Safety signals negative (f_03ebfcf3341563, f_9e63768b7d44f5, f_acf8d8c84c115a). Supratherapeutic dose (600 mg) vs trial dose (130 mg) limits relevance.

hypotheses.would_settle: SBP data at therapeutic 130 mg dose in phase 3 (not in verified facts).

for.text: High-risk vascular disease patients on background statin therapy (f_9d1ad54c100105, f_32b6ffda311f74). Events may be driven by processes less responsive to CETP inhibition (e.g., plaque rupture, thrombosis) rather than lipid progression.

against.text: Population similar to other lipid-lowering outcome trials (e.g., statin, PCSK9 inhibitor trials) that showed benefit. No evidence this population is uniquely unresponsive to LDL-C lowering.

hypotheses.would_settle: Subgroup analysis by baseline LDL-C, prior events, or statin intensity in ACCELERATE (not available).

for.text: Composite endpoint includes coronary revascularization and hospitalization for unstable angina — softer endpoints that may dilute treatment effect on hard events (CV death, MI, stroke) (f_32b6ffda311f74, f_6ee2720edb58bf).

Median follow-up 1.5 years (f_13d6532df5671c), event-driven but stopped early for futility (f_4657510a19768e). Short follow-up may miss late benefit of HDL-C elevation (if causal) or plaque stabilization.

against.text: Other lipid trials (IMPROVE-IT, FOURIER, ODYSSEY) showed benefit within 2-3 years on similar composites. Endpoint composition not unique.

hypotheses.would_settle: Component-specific HRs from ACCELERATE (not in verified facts).

for.text: Trial stopped early for futility by independent DMC (f_4657510a19768e, f_a92d2049d72b37). This is a scientific execution decision, not a business decision, but it prevented full event accrual (planned 1670 events, f_7262d7298b3588).

against.text: Stopping for futility is appropriate when conditional power is low. No evidence of poor adherence, recruitment, or sponsor interference.

hypotheses.would_settle: DMC charter and conditional power analysis at interim (not in verified facts).

for.text: No placebo-adjusted phase 3 biomarker data at 130 mg dose (critic feedback). Phase 3 within-arm changes (LDL-C -14%/-36%, HDL-C +129%/+54%) likely overestimate true drug effect. Calculator relied on phase 2 data at different dose/regimen (100 mg monotherapy or 100 mg + atorvastatin vs active comparator).
apoB and SBP data only at supratherapeutic 600 mg Day 14 (f_5d42a0b83c3256, f_049dd7f5983efe), not at therapeutic dose or duration.

hypotheses.would_settle: Full ACCELERATE publication or FDA review with placebo-adjusted lipid/apoB/SBP changes at 130 mg.
